name: Korean Radish

companions.note: Daikon-type radishes repel flea beetles that attack brassicas
Compatible fall timing; spinach fills gaps between radish plants

pnw_notes: Korean Bora King is a purple-skinned daikon-type radish with crisp white flesh — a staple of Korean cooking and kimchi. Much larger and slower than salad radishes; needs loose, deep soil to form properly. Fall is the prime window in the PNW. Store roots in a cool place after harvest; keeps for weeks.

frost_hardiness.notes: Large root is insulated through a Portland winter. Tops die back in hard freeze; harvest the root anytime until ground freezes.

planting_windows.notes: Spring window; harvest before summer heat
Primary fall window — 50–60 days before first frost; deep, loose soil essential
Spring harvest; pull before ground heats up
Fall harvest; roots store well in a cool place for weeks
